outcome: Tao Li, Yoav Moriah and Tali Pinsky's proof that tunnel number one knots satisfying a lens space surgery are Berge knots -- a restricted case of the stated conjecture -- was formally accepted and published in a refereed journal (Geometry & Topology, vol. 29, no. 6, 2025) within the window, and the arXiv preprint received a final revision (v7, 1 November 2024) also within the window; but the mathematical claim itself, and a proof of it, were already publicly posted as v1 in January 2017, well before the frozen revision date, so the substance of the result predates the window and only its expert vetting/publication falls inside it. The general Berge conjecture (for arbitrary knots in S^3) remains open.
summary: The bullet as stated ("the only knots in the 3-sphere which admit lens space surgeries are Berge knots") remains open in full generality; no result in the window settles it for all knots. What did happen in the window concerns a restricted case: Li, Moriah and Pinsky's paper 'Tunnel number one knots satisfy the Berge Conjecture' (arXiv:1701.01421), which shows that a tunnel number one knot in S^3 admitting a non-trivial lens space surgery must be doubly primitive, i.e. a Berge knot -- confirming the conjecture for that sub-class. This is a genuine case of the stated problem (a restriction to tunnel number one knots), not a variant, so under §3.1 it counts as `partial` progress toward the whole conjecture. The complication is dating: v1 of this paper, making exactly this claim with a purported proof, was posted 5 January 2017 -- seven years before the frozen revision. v3 was withdrawn in September 2018 (apparently over a gap), and the paper was repaired and reposted as v4 in December 2019, still years before the window. It sat as an unrefereed, long-standing preprint claim through the frozen revision date. What happened inside the window (26 Jan 2024 to today) is: a further arXiv revision (v6, April 2023, just before the window, followed by v7, 1 November 2024, inside the window) and, decisively, formal peer-reviewed publication in Geometry & Topology in 2025 -- a top journal in the field, which entails expert referee review of the argument. That refereeing is the event that converts a long-outstanding, twice-revised preprint claim into an expert-digested result, which is what makes `resolved` rather than `claimed` appropriate for this sub-case, and it happened inside the window even though the underlying mathematical content was substantially already public in 2017-2019. I found no AI involvement anywhere in this history: the paper's acknowledgements thank named mathematicians (Berge, Baker, Zupan, Rolfsen) for remarks, with no mention of any computational or AI tool. A tangential hit, a GitHub issue in Google DeepMind's 'formal-conjectures' repository proposing to formalize the Berge conjecture statement in Lean, is purely a cataloguing request (the issue itself says knot theory is missing from mathlib, so it cannot even be stated yet) with no proof attempt, and the issue text discloses it was itself drafted by an AI agent and human-reviewed -- irrelevant to the mathematics and correctly ai_role `none`. I searched separately for any progress on the general conjecture (Floer-homology approaches by Baker-Grigsby-Hedden, Greene's simple-knot classification) and found nothing new in the window beyond restatements of pre-2024 work.
competing_reading: One could argue this should be `open_stale`, on the reasoning that the decisive mathematical fact (tunnel-number-one knots satisfying the surgery are doubly primitive) was already established and publicly claimed with a full proof by 2019 (v4), so nothing new was mathematically discovered in the window -- only a paper that had been sitting on arXiv for years finally got a journal's stamp. Under a strict reading of §6.3 ("date the first public written argument... never the journal publication"), the first written argument is 2017/2019, which would make this `open_stale`. I did not choose that reading because `resolved` under §6.1 explicitly requires an argument that has been digested by experts (via journal acceptance or expert digestion), and that expert vetting genuinely did not occur until the 2024-2025 window -- the paper spent 2019-2023 as an unrefereed, once-withdrawn preprint, which is not equivalent in evidentiary weight to a refereed proof in Geometry & Topology. I treat the 2025 publication (preceded by the Nov 2024 arXiv revision, presumably incorporating referee-requested fixes) as the event that makes this specific case newly `resolved`-grade evidence, while flagging that the raw claim is much older.
what_would_settle_it: Access to the referee reports or a diff between v6 (April 2023) and v7 (November 2024) would show whether the November 2024 revision fixed a substantive gap found in refereeing (supporting dating the event to 2024-2025) or was a purely cosmetic change for publication (supporting `open_stale` with the real event dated to 2019/v4). Comment from the authors or the Geometry & Topology editors on the referee process would resolve this.
